problem: Revenue dropped sharply and the company needed to reduce costs.
title: Airbnb cuts about a quarter of its workforce and refocuses on its core
context: Travel collapsed in 2020 and Airbnb expected 2020 revenue to fall below half of 2019's.
decision_made: Lay off about 1,900 employees, around 25 percent, and pause investments outside the core business such as transportation and an entertainment studio.
action_taken: Chesky's memo offered 14 weeks of base pay plus one week per year of service.
observed_outcome: Second-quarter 2020 revenue was down 72 percent year over year, and the company reported some profitable quarters, including Q3, in its November 2020 IPO filing.
lessons: Cutting to a focused core during a shock can preserve the business, but the human cost is large.
limitations: Headcount differs slightly by source. The filing reports results but does not isolate the effect of the layoffs.

claims.claim_text: Airbnb said about 1,900 employees, around 25 percent of the company, would leave.
Airbnb's IPO filing showed Q2 2020 revenue down 72 percent and some profitable quarters.
